- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for the next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model often overcorrects downward; cap downward revisions to 50% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 5–15% to forecast for 3–7 days ahead.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is >2.5x true mean, reduce by 30–50% in next 3–5 days; if <0.5x, increase by 20–40%.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early (first 5–7 days) and underestimates late (last 5–7 days); apply asymmetric smoothing: reduce early forecast by 15–25%, increase late by 10–20%.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.00/0.67), model fails to capture momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of 3–5 prior days to anchor forecast.
